missions.name: Bomber Training: South Wales
missions.brief: A training sortie for bomber crews. Take off from RAF Hurn, Bournemouth, and climb away west along the Channel until the Bristol Channel opens up ahead. Five practice targets are laid out across South Wales: Swansea Docks, the Llandarcy oil refinery, Cardiff Docks, the Cardiff railway yards and Newport Docks. Press N for the bombsight: dial the speed and altitude shown on your instruments so the hit marker is true, then release when the target is in the sight. There are no enemy fighters on this run. When all five are down, turn for home and land back at Hurn.

missions.name: Battle of Britain: Kent Skies
missions.brief: Mid-August 1940. Waves of Stukas and Heinkels escorted by Bf 109s head across the Channel at Kent's radar stations and airfields. Scramble from Biggin Hill, break up the raid before it reaches the coast. (Axis: smash the Chain Home radar and Short Brothers works.)

missions.name: Operation Jubilee: Dieppe
missions.brief: Dawn, 19 August 1942. Canadian troops land at Dieppe. Provide fighter cover and suppress shore batteries from Tangmere against the new Focke-Wulf 190s. (Axis: intercept the landing force and its fighter umbrella.)

(Axis: a handful of Fw 190s against the sky full of Allied fighters.)

missions.name: D-Day: Utah Beach, First Light
missions.brief: Sixth of June, before dawn. Four thousand ships are off the Cotentin. At Utah Beach the Fourth Division goes ashore at half past six. Your job is to silence the batteries at Azeville and Crisbecq, and the guns on the Pointe du Hoc, before the first landing craft touch down. Marauders go in first, rocket Typhoons after. Look for the smoke and for the boats in the water below you, and do not hit our own ships. (Axis: Alarm! The invasion has begun. Landing craft are heading for the coast in their hundreds under a roof of fighters.)

events.text: The fleet is below you. Battleships are firing, look at the flashes on the horizon.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: THE FLEET

events.text: The first boats are running in. Hit the batteries before they reach the sand.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: LANDING CRAFT

missions.name: D-Day: Omaha, H-Hour
missions.brief: H-Hour at Omaha, and it is going badly. The bombers dropped too far inland and the German strongpoints are untouched. The first waves are pinned on the beach below the bluffs. Hit the strongpoint at Colleville, the Pointe du Hoc, and the Longues battery that still has the fleet under fire. Come in low, the cloud is at two thousand, and keep clear of the naval gunfire. (Axis: The Americans are landing at Omaha, but our coast guns have them pinned on the beach. If you can break up the second wave of landing craft, the first will be thrown back into the sea.)

events.text: Heavy fire on Omaha. The infantry are pinned on the shingle. Every bunker you hit is a hundred lives.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: OMAHA

missions.name: D-Day: Gold, Juno and Sword
missions.brief: By half past seven the British and Canadians are going ashore on three beaches, with the tanks swimming in beside the infantry. Rockets and bombs on the strongpoints at Mont Fleury, Courseulles and Riva Bella, and the big guns at Longues that still reach the fleet. Then keep the Fw 190s off the beach. Visibility is perfect: you will see the whole invasion laid out below you. (Axis: The British are landing on a front of twenty miles and our coast batteries are the only thing holding them. Protect the strongpoints at Mont Fleury, Courseulles and Riva Bella from the bombers and Typhoons.)

events.text: Landing craft by the hundred. The British and Canadian beaches are in front of you.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: THE BEACHES

events.text: Sword is under fire from Riva Bella. Hit it.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: RIVA BELLA

missions.name: D-Day: Night of the Airborne
missions.brief: Just after midnight, sixth of June. Six Horsa gliders are about to land beside the canal bridges at Benouville, and the Merville battery must be silenced before it can fire on the beaches at dawn. Strike the targets on the pathfinders' marks, then draw the night fighters away from the transport stream. It is dark, with a good moon. Keep radio silence over the coast. (Axis: Alarm! Strong formations are over the Cotentin in the dark and parachutes are falling south of Caen. Night-fighter crews are to take off at once and engage the transport stream.)

events.text: Pathfinders are on the ground. Gliders are cast off over the coast.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: THE AIRBORNE

events.text: Searchlights on the right. Light flak over Ranville. Keep your height.
events.speaker: Navigator
events.label: FLAK

missions.name: D-Day: The Beachhead
missions.brief: Noon over the beachhead. Troops, tanks and guns are coming ashore at every beach and the Luftwaffe knows it. A handful of Fw 190s are trying to get through the patrols. Defend the invasion fleet. Stay at medium height, keep your eyes on the low ground, and do not follow anyone down into our own flak. (Axis: Sixth of June, noon. The sky is not ours, but we are told the fleet must be hit.)

events.text: The fleet is unloading. Barrage balloons over the transports. Remember your recognition stripes.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: ON PATROL

missions.name: D-Day: The Panzer Counter-Attack
missions.brief: Evening of D-Day. The Twenty-first Panzer Division is rolling north from Caen to throw the British back into the sea. A column of tanks and half-tracks is on the Biéville road. Typhoons with rockets, Thunderbolts with bombs: hit the column before it reaches Sword. Strafe first, then rockets, and watch for flak wagons in the column. (Axis: Twenty-first Panzer is moving on Sword, our one real chance to throw the English back into the sea. The enemy fighter-bombers are over the road and the column must get through.)

events.text: Twenty-first Panzer is on the road from Caen, tanks in the open. Roads are dusty, they will be easy to see.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: PANZERS

events.text: Smoke on the road. That is the lead column.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: LEAD COLUMN

missions.name: D-Day: Mulberry at Dusk
missions.brief: Nine days after the landings, the Mulberry harbour at Arromanches is nearly ready, and the Luftwaffe knows it. Their bombers are coming in at dusk, out of the sun, heading for the supply ships. It is the same trick as every night this week. Patrol over the harbour, break up the raid, and bring the bombers down before they release. (Axis: Ninth of June. The Allies have built an artificial harbour off Arromanches and every day it unloads more tanks and guns than we can destroy.)

events.text: The harbour is almost finished. Sunken blockships make a breakwater, and every stone is covered in guns.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: MULBERRY

missions.name: Dunkirk: First Light
missions.brief: Twenty-eighth of May. The army is being pushed back onto the Dunkirk beaches and there is a thick fog on the coast. In the fog, the navy and the little ships are lifting men off. Patrol the coast, find the Stukas before they reach the evacuation ships, and stay out of the cloud over the town. The Hurricanes will cover the east beaches. Good hunting. (Axis: The British are trapped against the sea at Dunkirk and the Führer has halted the panzers. It is up to the Luftwaffe to finish the job from the air.)

events.text: The Channel is full of boats. Destroyers, ferries, tugs and fishing smacks, all heading for the beaches.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: THE LITTLE SHIPS

missions.name: Dunkirk: The Mole
missions.brief: Twenty-ninth of May. The East Mole is the best way off the beach: a mile of jetty with a destroyer on each side, taking a thousand men at a time. The Stukas know it. Everything depends on keeping them off the Mole. Climb to angels fifteen, find the dive bombers before they start their dives, and never mind the escort. (Axis: The Mole at Dunkirk is the key to the evacuation: a long concrete jetty at which the destroyers can load a thousand men an hour. If we sink a ship alongside it, we block it.)

events.text: The Mole is crowded with men. A destroyer is alongside, loading from both sides.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: THE MOLE

missions.name: Dunkirk: The Perimeter
missions.brief: Thirty-first of May. Our infantry are holding a perimeter around the port with rifles and a handful of guns, and German armour is closing in from the south. Hurricanes and Spitfires are to strafe the column on the Bergues road. Fly low, hit the lorries and the tanks, and climb away before the flak finds you. (Axis: Thirty-first of May. Our panzers and infantry are advancing on the port from the south.)

events.text: German armour is closing on the perimeter at Bergues. The army is holding with rifles and anti-tank guns.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: THE PERIMETER

events.text: Tanks to the south of the canal. They are in the open.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: PANZERS

missions.name: Dunkirk: The Night Raid
missions.brief: Night of the thirtieth. The evacuation continues in the dark, with the burning oil tanks lighting the beaches. The Heinkels are coming to finish the job. Defiants and Hurricanes: patrol the harbour at night, find the bombers by their exhaust glow and bring them down before they bomb the ships. Do not use your landing lights. (Axis: Night of the thirtieth. The enemy evacuates in the dark and every ship that leaves is a battle lost.)

events.text: The oil tanks are still burning. The glow is visible from a hundred miles. Follow it.
events.speaker: Navigator
events.label: THE GLOW

events.text: Searchlights and tracer over the harbour. Light flak on the Mole.
events.speaker: Crew
events.label: FLAK

missions.name: Dunkirk: Black Friday
missions.brief: First of June, the worst day of the evacuation. The sun is out and the Luftwaffe knows it. The Stukas are coming in all day, wave after wave, and the destroyers and troopships are taking terrible losses. Every Spitfire we can put up is needed. Stay over the ships, fight the Stukas before they dive, and keep going until you run out of ammunition. (Axis: First of June. Clear skies at last, and the enemy is still lifting men from the beaches.)

events.text: Stukas in the sun. A great stack of them, nine thousand feet. Dive bombers over the ships.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: STUKAS

missions.name: Dunkirk: The Gun Line
missions.brief: Second of June. German heavy guns at Gravelines and at Nieuport are shelling the escape route, and the destroyers have to run past them to reach the beaches. Blenheims will bomb them from medium height. The cloud will give you cover to the coast, but it breaks up over the target. Keep a tight formation and let the escort do its work. (Axis: Second of June. Our heavy guns at Gravelines and Nieuport are shelling the English embarkation, but the English bombers will try to silence them.)

events.text: Heavy guns on the coast at Gravelines. Their shells are hitting the Mole and the Dunkirk roads.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: HEAVY GUNS

missions.name: Dunkirk: The Last Day
missions.brief: Fourth of June, before dawn. The last of the army is going aboard, and the rearguard is still on the Mole. Three hundred thousand men have been taken off, and the Admiralty has ordered the last ships to leave with the dawn. The Luftwaffe will be back when the fog clears. One last patrol: keep them off the ships until the final boats are away. (Axis: The enemy is still on the beaches at dawn and his ships are loading the last men. If the fog clears, strike the last convoy off the Mole.)

events.text: The last ships are loading. The rearguard are holding the line at the Mole.
events.speaker: Control
events.label: THE LAST SHIPS

missions.name: ◆ Dawn Patrol over the Weald
missions.brief: Mist lies over the Weald as Pevensey reports plots building over the Channel. Climb out of Kenley and meet the first wave before it reaches the coast.

missions.name: ◆ Solent Watch
missions.brief: Ju 87s are diving on the Portsmouth approaches. Get above them from Tangmere and keep the dockyard intact.

missions.name: ◆ Convoy Peewit Cover
missions.brief: The Channel convoy is steaming past Dover with E-boats and Stukas in the area. Protect the ships from Hawkinge.

missions.name: ◆ Night Over the Estuary
missions.brief: A night raid is heading up the Thames for the oil depots at Thameshaven. Find the bombers by their engine glow and break them up.

missions.name: ◆ East Coast Sweep
missions.brief: Fighter Command wants the sky cleared off the Suffolk coast. Sweep out from Duxford and engage whatever flies.

missions.name: ◆ Steel for the Ruhr
missions.brief: A medium-bomber raid on the Essen works, flown in daylight with fighter cover that may not stay with you the whole way.

missions.name: ◆ Hamm Marshalling Yard
missions.brief: Break the main rail artery feeding the front. Cloud helps on the approach and hurts on the run-in.

missions.name: ◆ Scholven Oil
missions.brief: Synthetic fuel keeps the Luftwaffe flying. Hit the Scholven plant and return before the fighters regroup.

missions.name: ◆ Waal Crossing
missions.brief: Suppress the defenders on the approaches to the Waal bridge so the ground column can cross.

missions.name: ◆ Scheldt Barges
missions.brief: The enemy still moves supplies by water around the Scheldt. Rocket and cannon the barge traffic at low level.

missions.name: ◆ Venlo Flak Belt
missions.brief: Dive-bomb the flak belt at Venlo and strafe the guns that survive.

missions.name: ◆ Lines of Supply
missions.brief: Dawn fog hides the supply trains. Find them on the rails near Spa before the haze lifts.

missions.name: ◆ Schiphol Sweep
missions.brief: A free-ranging sweep across Holland to pull the Luftwaffe up where you can fight it.

missions.name: ◆ Coastal Raid on Dover
missions.brief: Strike the radar at Dover and the harbour behind it. The RAF will rise to meet you.

missions.name: ◆ Dusk on the Thames
missions.brief: A long run up the estuary to the Royal Docks as the light fails. Fighters will be waiting.

missions.name: ◆ Hold the Bridges
missions.brief: Allied fighter-bombers are working over the Maas crossings. Stop them.

missions.name: ◆ Jet Hunt
missions.brief: Use the speed advantage to slash through the escorts and pick off bombers.

missions.name: ◆ Defence of the Reich
missions.brief: American medium bombers are heading for the oil plant and the marshalling yard. Get up from Rheine and turn them back.

missions.name: ◆ Winter Patrol
missions.brief: Low cloud over the Dutch border. Patrol the lines and catch any transports trying to slip through.

missions.name: ◆ Free Sweep
missions.brief: Roam across the Rhineland and clear the sky of fighters ahead of the afternoon bombers.

missions.name: ◆ Armour on the Road
missions.brief: A German armoured column is moving along the Geldern road. Rocket the vehicles and keep the road closed.

missions.name: ◆ Escort to Dusseldorf
missions.brief: Cover the bomber stream to Dusseldorf and bring it home. Fighters will hit from the north as you turn for the target.

missions.name: ◆ Cologne Alarm
missions.brief: Fighter-bombers are over the Rhine. Defend the bridge and the marshalling yard.

missions.name: ◆ Night Interception
missions.brief: Use the jet's speed against a night bomber stream heading for the rail junction and the chemical works.

missions.name: ◆ Column Strike
missions.brief: An Allied supply column is rolling along the front near Goch. Strafe it, then break for home before the fighters arrive.
